name: Rejoin the Fight
oracle_text: Mill three cards. Then starting with the next opponent in turn order, each opponent chooses a creature card in your graveyard that hasn't been chosen. Return each card chosen this way to the battlefield under your control.
blocked_sentences: Then starting with the next opponent in turn order, each opponent chooses a creature card in your graveyard that hasn't been chosen.
Return each card chosen this way to the battlefield under your control.

needs.what: a selector `chooser` that can name an arbitrary player -- a player spec such as {"binding": "each_player"} or "opponent" -- so that inside a `for_each_player` loop the looped opponent is the one asked to pick from a pool of cards that are in YOUR graveyard (and hence owned and controlled by you)
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `chooser` in `selector_keys` is validated at load time to exactly "controller", "owner" or "none" (selectors.validate_selector). For a pool of `{"zone": "graveyard", "controller": "you"}` both "controller" and "owner" resolve to the spell's controller, so the caster picks the creature cards instead of each opponent. `for_each_player` binds `each_player` only for the selector's `controller`/`player` filters, not for who is asked; `scry` is the only op with a separate `chooser` player spec and it is hard-wired to scry/fateseal, not to object selection.

needs.what: a way for a sequence of choices made in one resolution to accumulate, so a later choice can exclude everything already chosen -- e.g. an `as` binding on the choosing op that APPENDS across `for_each_player` iterations, readable by `exclude_binding`, giving "a creature card in your graveyard that hasn't been chosen"
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `exclude_binding` reads a binding written once by `as`, and `return_from_graveyard` sets no binding at all; even ops that do write `as` overwrite it each iteration, so iteration N could only exclude iteration N-1's pick, not the whole set. Nothing in `selector_keys` records "already chosen this resolution".

needs.what: choices gathered from several players first and the effect applied once to the whole set -- "each opponent chooses ... Return EACH card chosen this way to the battlefield" is one simultaneous return after all choices are made
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The only player-shaped loop, `for_each_player`, executes its whole body per player, so a `return_from_graveyard` inside it returns each creature as its own event; the cards would enter one at a time between choices rather than together, changing enters-the-battlefield ordering and letting each opponent see the previous card already on the battlefield.
